answers.1: Yellow + Green — both are people-oriented, warm and relationship-focused, so they click socially.
answers.2: Red + Blue — both are task-oriented (results + accuracy) and respect each other's focus on getting things done properly.
answers.3: Red — the dominant, decisive type wants control and the leadership seat.
answers.4: Blue — precision, procedure, high standards and attention to detail (a Red-Blue blend adds the decisiveness needed under pressure).
answers.5: Yellow — loves the spotlight, an audience and talking.
answers.6: Blue — systematic, orderly filing and records.
answers.7: Blue — needs data, analysis and verification before committing.
answers.8: Blue — punctuality is a rule and a matter of respect (Green is also dependable, but Blue is clock-precise).
answers.9: Red — results matter more than the rulebook.
answers.10: Red — will take risks and try untested shortcuts if it gets the result (Yellow supplies the novel ideas).
answers.11: Green — takes things personally, internalises hurt and remembers it for years.
answers.12: Yellow — chaotic desk, but a huge network and knows who/where to ask.
answers.13: Red — decides fast and wants the authority to decide.
answers.15: Red — thrives on challenge, competition and obstacles to conquer.
answers.16: Red — snap judgments, fast and blunt conclusions about people (Blue judges too, but only after analysis against its standards).
answers.17: All four together — Red drives, Yellow energises/sells, Green supports and stabilises, Blue ensures quality; no single pair is 'best'.
answers.18: Yellow — talkative, expressive, thinks out loud.
answers.19: Yellow — quick, intuitive, enthusiastic about new ideas (Red is equally fast but filters for usefulness).
answers.20: Blue — perfectionist; can't trust anyone else to do it to standard, so re-does it (Red may also interfere out of impatience).
answers.22: Blue — reads and follows every step, including the last one.
answers.23: No single answer — it depends on the individual; people tend to gather others similar (or complementary) to their own profile.
